item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos couldn't pull out a tight one Tuesday night, dropping a 3-2 decision to the Columbus Clingstones in the opening game of their final regular-season road series.

The matchup turned into a pitcher's duel, with Clingstones starter Zebrowski keeping Pensacola's bats relatively quiet through most of the contest. Despite the low-scoring affair, the Blue Wahoos managed to stay competitive throughout, but ultimately came up one run short in the loss.

The defeat marks another tight game for Pensacola as the team winds down its regular season on the road. The Blue Wahoos will continue their series against Columbus as they look to bounce back in upcoming games.

The station has built a reputation as a community-focused outlet, and these nominations underscore its reach and influence in the Pensacola market.

item.title: Heat Index Climbing to 106° Wednesday; Rain Chances Increase

item.content:encoded:
Northwest Florida residents should prepare for dangerously hot conditions Wednesday, with the National Weather Service forecasting a heat index that could reach 106 degrees across the North Escambia area.

While afternoon highs are expected near 93 degrees, the combination of heat and humidity will make it feel significantly hotter. There's a 30 percent chance of scattered showers and thunderstorms between 1 p.m. and 4 p.m. Wednesday, though most of the day should remain sunny.

Rain chances will pick up heading into the latter part of the week, with increasing shower and storm potential through Friday. Anyone spending time outdoors Wednesday is urged to stay hydrated, take frequent breaks in air conditioning, and check on vulnerable family members and neighbors during the peak heat hours.

item.title: Florida Man Executed 50 Years After 1974 Murder
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Harold Gene Lucas, 74, was executed by lethal injection Tuesday evening at Florida State Prison, more than five decades after killing 16-year-old Jill Piper in her Bonita Springs home. Lucas was pronounced dead at 6:18 p.m., according to the Florida Department of Corrections. The case spanned 50 years from the 1974 crime to Tuesday's execution.…
item.content:encoded:
Harold Gene Lucas, 74, was executed by lethal injection Tuesday evening at Florida State Prison, more than five decades after killing 16-year-old Jill Piper in her Bonita Springs home. Lucas was pronounced dead at 6:18 p.m., according to the Florida Department of Corrections.

The case spanned 50 years from the 1974 crime to Tuesday's execution. Lucas waived his remaining appeals and chose not to contest the death sentence, effectively allowing the execution to proceed without further legal challenge.

The execution marks the conclusion of one of Florida's longest-running capital cases, reflecting the often-lengthy appellate process in death penalty cases within the state corrections system.

item.content:encoded:
The Century Town Council has approved a zero-interest repayment agreement with the Florida Department of Transportation for utility relocation costs along Highway 29, totaling $522,555.71.

The council voted on the revised promissory note during a brief Tuesday night meeting that lasted just seven to eight minutes. The agreement allows the town to spread out payments for the relocation expenses without accruing interest.

Utility relocation projects like the one on Highway 29 are typically required when state transportation improvements demand that power lines, water lines, and other infrastructure be moved to accommodate road work. The zero-interest arrangement helps smaller municipalities manage the significant costs associated with these necessary relocations.

item.title: Local police suspend license plate reader program following state directive
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Both the Escambia County Sheriff's Office and Pensacola Police Department have suspended their use of Automated License Plate Recognition (ALPR) camera networks, according to announcements made Tuesday. The local action follows a statewide directive issued Monday by Gov. Ron DeSantis' administration. ALPR systems use cameras to automatically…
item.content:encoded:
Both the Escambia County Sheriff's Office and Pensacola Police Department have suspended their use of Automated License Plate Recognition (ALPR) camera networks, according to announcements made Tuesday. The local action follows a statewide directive issued Monday by Gov. Ron DeSantis' administration.

ALPR systems use cameras to automatically capture and record license plate information from vehicles, a technology that has been deployed by law enforcement agencies across Florida for investigative purposes. The suspension affects both agencies' ability to utilize the camera networks for ongoing operations.

The state-level decision to suspend ALPR operations represents a significant shift in how Florida law enforcement conducts vehicle tracking and investigation. Details regarding the duration of the suspension or the specific reasoning behind the state directive were not immediately available from either local agency.

Both ECSO and PPD have not yet announced when the suspension might be lifted or whether alternative methods will be implemented to replace the technology's investigative capabilities.

item.title: Mobile Students Launch Website to Connect Homeless with Vetted Boarding Homes
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A new online platform developed by students in Mobile is tackling one of the area's most pressing social challenges: homelessness. According to WKRG News 5, the website helps connect people experiencing homelessness with vetted boarding homes in the region, where an estimated 3,000 residents currently lack stable housing. Local advocates working…
item.content:encoded:
A new online platform developed by students in Mobile is tackling one of the area's most pressing social challenges: homelessness. According to WKRG News 5, the website helps connect people experiencing homelessness with vetted boarding homes in the region, where an estimated 3,000 residents currently lack stable housing.

Local advocates working on the issue say the real barrier to solving homelessness often isn't money alone—it's access to reliable resources and information. The student-built platform aims to fill that gap by creating a searchable database of available housing options and helping match individuals with appropriate placements.

One user of the service, Isaiah Bruce, told WKRG the website has been transformative for his situation. "It really has changed my life," he said. The platform's emphasis on vetting boarding home operators is designed to ensure safety and quality for vulnerable users seeking stable housing.

item.content:encoded:
The Port City Classic, a popular HBCU football matchup, is coming back to Mobile this Labor Day weekend with Tuskegee University taking on Fort Valley State University at Ladd-Peebles Stadium. According to WKRG News 5, kickoff is scheduled for 4 p.m. Saturday.

Beyond the game itself, organizers have lined up a full slate of events to celebrate the occasion. The festivities include a parade, a concert, and an HBCU summit—all designed to draw fans and build excitement around the matchup.

Thursday's events kick off at 9 a.m., though organizers have scheduled activities throughout the weekend leading up to Saturday's game. For Pensacola-area football fans looking to head over to Mobile for the holiday weekend, the Port City Classic offers a chance to catch quality college football while enjoying the broader celebration of historically Black colleges and universities.

According to event organizers, the gathering will bring together community members and firefighters to reflect on the tragic events of 2001 and pay tribute to the courage displayed in the aftermath of the attacks. The observance continues a tradition of remembrance across Northwest Florida, where firefighters and emergency personnel regularly mark the anniversary.

Details about the specific date, time, and location of the event were not immediately available. Community members interested in attending the commemoration are encouraged to reach out to the Santa Rosa County Firefighters' Association for more information.

The widower is now sharing how his late wife's contributions to cancer research may help future patients facing the same diagnosis. Pancreatic cancer remains one of…
item.content:encoded:
A newly approved pancreatic cancer medication represents a milestone that one Baldwin County woman hoped to witness during her own battle with the disease, according to WKRG News 5. The widower is now sharing how his late wife's contributions to cancer research may help future patients facing the same diagnosis.

Pancreatic cancer remains one of the most aggressive forms of the disease, with survival rates significantly lower than many other cancers. The newly approved drug offers some patients the potential for extended survival time, a development that could impact treatment options across the Southeast and beyond.

While the Baldwin County woman did not live to see the medication's approval, her family says her participation in clinical trials and advocacy for research helped pave the way for this breakthrough. Stories like hers highlight how individual patients contribute to the broader scientific effort to combat cancer.

item.content:encoded:
Two Gulf Breeze residents face animal cruelty charges after a neighbor's video captured abuse of their two bulldogs, according to Santa Rosa County authorities.

Charolette Dellinger and David Neely, both 57, were arrested following the incident. Santa Rosa County Chief Deputy Randy Tifft emphasized the importance of stepping away from frustration with pets rather than resorting to violence.

"You get frustrated with your pet, you just walk away from it," Tifft said, underscoring the department's message about responsible pet ownership and anger management.

The case highlights how community vigilance can protect animals. Authorities encourage residents to report suspected animal abuse to local law enforcement.

item.content:encoded:

Hudspeth's squad continues to build momentum heading into the remainder of the regular season.

item.title: Woman Gets Time Served in Child Abduction Case After Mexico Flight
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A woman who took her daughter across the border to Mexico has been sentenced to time served in an international parental kidnapping case, according to WKRG News 5. Haley Harris was convicted after she fled Alabama with her child in September 2025, crossing into Mexico with the girl. The case drew authorities from multiple jurisdictions as law…
item.content:encoded:
A woman who took her daughter across the border to Mexico has been sentenced to time served in an international parental kidnapping case, according to WKRG News 5.

Haley Harris was convicted after she fled Alabama with her child in September 2025, crossing into Mexico with the girl. The case drew authorities from multiple jurisdictions as law enforcement worked to locate and recover the child.

Harris received a sentence of time served, meaning the time she already spent in custody counted as her full punishment. The resolution concludes a case that highlighted the serious federal crimes involved when a custodial parent unlawfully removes a child across international lines.

Details about the circumstances surrounding the abduction and the child's recovery were not immediately available.

item.content:encoded: Cat Country 98.7 and the Cat Pak Morning Show have both been nominated for 2026 Country Music Association awards. Cat Country is one of five radio stations nationwide nominated for Radio Station of the Year, while the Cat Pak Morning Show is one of five nominees for Broadcast Personality of the Year. WYCT previously won Station of the Year in 2017, 2019 and 2024, while the Cat Pak Morning Show won Broadcast Personality of the Year in 2022. The winners will be announced during the 60th Annual CMA Awards, which airs Nov. 19 on ABC.
